title: Saturday dance
text: At the dance on Saturday, {t.name} asks you for a dance. Then another. By the third, your friends have stopped pretending not to look.

success.text: {t.name} walks you home. On Sunday, {t.he} calls.

failure.text: By the last song, {t.name} is dancing with someone else.

choices.result: You think about {t.him} on the bus home anyway.

title: A dinner party
text: Your friends have planned this, and they are not subtle about it: at dinner you are seated next to {t.name}, who is also single. Everyone else leaves early.

success.text: You have dinner again the week after, just the two of you. Your friends are unbearable about it.

failure.text: {t.name} is lovely, and very clear that {t.he} is not looking for anything right now.

choices.result: Your friends sigh. You help with the dishes.

title: Stuck
text: The train stops between two stations and stays there for an hour. By the time it moves again, you and {t.name}, a stranger in the next seat, have told each other things you've never told anyone.

success.text: {t.name} writes {t.his} number on your ticket. You keep the ticket for years.

failure.text: {t.name} smiles. "Some things are better as one hour on a train."

choices.result: You look for {t.him} on that train for weeks.

title: A match
text: {t.name} has sent you a message on a dating app. It's actually funny – and {t.he} has read the same book you're reading.

success.text: One drink becomes four. You both delete the app a month later.

failure.text: {t.name} was funnier in writing. So, apparently, were you.

choices.result: There's always someone else. That's the problem.
